articles_hidden.title: Adiós al notario de por vida: cómo la Ley N° 21.772 reescribe la fe pública, el Registro Conservatorio y la tradición de los inmuebles
articles_hidden.authors: Andrés Gabriel Varas Quijón
articles_hidden.abstract:
La Ley N° 21.772, publicada el 1 de octubre de 2025 y vigente desde el 2 de abril de 2026, es la
reforma más profunda del sistema notarial y registral chileno desde el Código Orgánico de Tribunales:
reemplaza las designaciones discrecionales por concursos del Sistema de Alta Dirección Pública, pone fin a
los cargos vitalicios con un límite de 75 años, veta a los familiares de determinadas autoridades, somete a
notarios, conservadores y archiveros a la Ley del Consumidor y a una fiscalización multicapa —fiscales
judiciales, auditorías externas, SERNAC—, impone transparencia activa, precios máximos, horarios
obligatorios y estándares tecnológicos, y faculta al Presidente para dividir incluso el Conservador de
Santiago. Este trabajo deja la crónica a la prensa y se concentra en lo que la reforma cambia en el derecho
civil: el Reglamento del Registro Conservatorio de 1857 pasa a ser ley, cerrando un debate de siglo y medio
sobre su naturaleza; los notarios deberán remitir electrónicamente los títulos al Conservador sin
intervención de los interesados, salvo oposición o falta de pago, lo que ha hecho preguntar si la tradición
sigue siendo un acto bilateral — el artículo sostiene que sí, porque la voluntad traslaticia viaja dentro del
título y el requerimiento de inscripción es su mera ejecución, como la práctica ya sabía por la cláusula del
portador; las instrucciones notariales reciben por fin naturaleza legal de comisión de confianza y contrato; la
huella digital, las cifras y las copias remotas y gratuitas rediseñan la fe pública; y la Ley N° 19.799 marca el
límite de lo que puede ser digital. Se examinan las consecuencias prácticas para el estudio de títulos, las
promesas, los remates y la redacción de escrituras e instrucciones, y se cierra con un decálogo del usuario
prudente de la fe pública. La tesis: Bello imaginó en 1855 la propiedad territorial «a la vista de todos, en un
cuadro que representaría, por decirlo así, instantáneamente sus mutaciones»; la Ley N° 21.772 es, con ciento
setenta años de retraso, la pantalla de ese cuadro.

articles_hidden.title: From Himalayan Catastrophe to National Resilience: Lessons from the 2026 Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River Floods in Nepal
articles_hidden.authors: Keshav Bhattarai; Ambika P. Adhikari
articles_hidden.abstract:
The August 2026 Bhote Koshi–Trishuli disaster was not simply another flood. It was a cascading cryosphere disaster linking glacier instability, steep Himalayan topography, hydropower, highways, international trade, tourism, and pilgrimage—exposing weaknesses in transboundary observation, monitoring, and development planning (ICIMOD, 2026b; Reuters, 2026a). Nepal must treat it as a turning point.

On the morning of 26 August 2026, the mountains above Nepal’s northern frontier delivered a disaster of almost unimaginable speed and scale. A massive mass of ice, rock, and sediment detached in the high Himalayan terrain near the Nepal–Tibet border, descended roughly 1,200 metres, interacted with the Lhende Khola system, and generated a debris-rich flood that surged through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors, destroying settlements, markets, roads, bridges, hydropower facilities, and an international border crossing and transforming them into fields of mud, boulders, and wreckage within minutes (ICIMOD, 2026b; Reuters, 2026a). Satellite analysis indicates that a substantial section of glacier and adjoining rock detached from approximately 5,200 metres elevation, while river levels downstream rose by as much as seven to nine metres within approximately half an hour in some locations (ICIMOD, 2026b; The Guardian, 2026). That rate left extraordinarily little time for people to recognize the danger, much less to evacuate. Although some areas were warned via police megaphones, announcements by the local governments, and mobile alerts, most people took it as regular seasonal flood warnings and missed the opportunity to escape.

articles_hidden.title: САНКЦИИ КАК КАТАЛИЗАТОР РОСТА ВНУТРЕННЕГО ТУРИЗМА: ЭКОНОМИЧЕСКИЕ ПРОБЛЕМЫ И ПУТИ ИХ РЕШЕНИЯ РОССИИ
articles_hidden.authors: Զախար
articles_hidden.abstract: Статья посвящена анализу влияния международных санкций на развитие внутреннего туризма в России. Рассматриваются экономические последствия ограничения внешних туристических потоков и перераспределения спроса внутри страны. Особое внимание уделяется тому, как санкции стали стимулом для переориентации туризма на внутренний рынок, росту инвестиций в региональную инфраструктуру и формированию новых туристических продуктов. В работе анализируются ключевые экономические проблемы, возникающие в условиях санкционного давления, и предлагаются возможные решения, направленные на повышение устойчивости и конкурентоспособности Российского туристического сектора.

articles_hidden.title: Well-intended policy gone wrong? Voluntary Surrenders as a de facto amnesty for illegal wildlife use and trade in Colombia
articles_hidden.authors: Natalia Munoz Cassolis; Johana M. Herrera Montoya; Douglas MacMillan; Francisco Perera Rieder; Melissa Arias
articles_hidden.abstract: The illegal wildlife trade (IWT) has been the focus of numerous international and national legal frameworks aiming to counter the harms it poses to biodiversity. The enforcement of these laws typically involves the seizure or confiscation of wildlife specimens, which have become a common metric for IWT reporting and a proxy for estimating its scale. Another commonly used, but less understood mechanism is the Voluntary Surrender of wildlife specimens. Our research examines the legal implications and practical implementation of Voluntary Surrenders in Colombia, where this administrative mechanism was originally designed as a transitional educational tool to raise awareness of the environmental and welfare harms of illegal wildlife pet keeping, and to encourage individuals to relinquish illegally held specimens. Drawing on a thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with environmental legal experts, law enforcement officers, and conservation researchers and practitioners, we identified the typologies of actors and circumstances giving rise to Voluntary Surrenders, alongside the legal interpretation, implementation, and governance challenges linked to this mechanism. We demonstrate how this well-intentioned policy operates as a de facto amnesty for IWT in Colombia, enabling offenders to evade sanctions and law enforcement personnel to bypass burdensome sanctioning procedures. Consequently, Voluntary Surrenders have perpetuated impunity, normalized illicit wildlife possession, reinforced a notion of IWT as a non-serious crime, and obscured its true scale, as these incidents are systematically excluded from national and international reporting frameworks, such as the CITES Illegal Trade database. We conclude that an urgent revision of this regulatory framework is needed.

articles_hidden.title: Da ocupação declarada à posição social: as decisões de medida do pacote ocupacoesBR
articles_hidden.authors: Vitor de Moraes Peixoto
articles_hidden.abstract:
Nos registros administrativos brasileiros, a ocupação declarada é a principal via de acesso à posição
social de quem foi registrado. Ela não chega, porém, como medida: chega como código de um cadastro
construído para outra finalidade. Este artigo documenta a cadeia de decisões que converte esse código
em medida padronizada, tal como implementada no pacote ocupacoesBR, e apresenta a história das
classificações que tornam cada decisão necessária. O argumento central é que adotar uma classificação
internacional não dispensa decisões, apenas as desloca para pontos menos visíveis, e que elas podem
ser enunciadas como critérios verificáveis. Demonstra-se o procedimento no caso da fronteira entre
profissionais e técnicos, herdada de um juízo de 1988 sobre a formação típica de cada ocupação: em
vez de ajustar os casos que parecem errados, adota-se o critério de seguir a classificação onde ela
própria moveu o código entre versões, e verifica-se que a lista assim produzida é exaustiva. A medida
é validada, no nível da ocupação, contra o patrimônio e a escolaridade declarados pelas próprias
candidaturas. A correlação de 0,68 com o patrimônio mediano é a informativa das duas, por ser o
único critério externo à construção do índice. A de 0,76 com a proporção de candidatos com curso
superior é apenas verificação de consistência interna, porque a escolaridade entrou na construção do
índice. Três limites não admitem correção e são declarados. O índice de status foi estimado sobre
população masculina, e as ocupações majoritariamente femininas apresentam mais credencial e menos
status. O componente proprietário da classe alta não tem âncora em registro externo, ao contrário
do credenciado. E a raça, que opera de modo independente no topo da hierarquia, não é observável
por uma medida construída sobre ocupação

articles_hidden.title: AI in Science and its Implications: A Narrative Review
articles_hidden.authors: Philip Shapira; John Nelson; Julie Jebsen; Seoyoon Kang
articles_hidden.abstract: This narrative review synthesizes diverse empirical, technical, conceptual, and policy literature on the development and use of AI in science. Drawing on a sociology of science and technology framing, we examine how the adoption of AI may redistribute scientific work, expertise, epistemic authority, resources, and accountability across organizational and infrastructural contexts. The literature suggests three cross-cutting patterns. First, AI tends to redistribute rather than eliminate work, creating new demands for configuration, monitoring, interpretation, and validation. Second, gains in productivity and novelty are uneven and depend on problem characteristics, data, infrastructure, and complementary human expertise. Third, AI may shift authority and institutional power toward actors that develop, own, and govern models and computational resources. AI also raises contested questions about explanation, evidence, creativity, responsibility, inequality, and environmental costs. We identify priorities for research on the epistemic status of AI-generated knowledge, inequalities in access to infrastructure and training, disciplinary variations, changing forms of accountability and institutional authority, and the governance of AI in and for science.

articles_hidden.title: Faith in Action: Does Ramadan Reduce Crime?
articles_hidden.authors: Sk Niyaj Mohammed; Ashokankur Datta
articles_hidden.abstract: As a social institution, religion creates incentives or disincentives for ‘appropriate’ and ‘inappropriate’ social behaviour, including attitudes towards participation in criminal activities. The size of such an effect depends on the intensity of socio-religious norms regarding specific forms of crime. Ramadan, a period of heightened religiosity among Muslims, involves expectations regarding socially desirable behaviour among individuals. Ramadan also involves mandated fasting, which affects local economic activity. How do such expectations and religious restructuring of daily life affect the incidence of crime among believers directly and/or indirectly? Using a difference-in-differences methodology and information from a unique dataset of criminal offences, we estimate the impact of Ramadan on criminal offences committed by those affected by it. Our identification strategy leverages the shifting timing of Ramadan through the Gregorian calendar to isolate the causal effect from confounding seasonality. We find that Ramadan leads to economically and statistically significant reductions in both violent and non-violent crimes, with estimated effect sizes ranging from 8 to 23 percent. We find suggestive evidence of these results being mediated by changes in religiosity and associated behavioural norms rather than by labour market channels. Our results provide suggestive evidence that informal institutions, such as religion, may complement formal state institutions in efforts to reduce crime.

articles_hidden.title: Rock art of the Colombian Amazon: open access ground-based photographic imagery from the Serranía de La Lindosa (Guaviare Department, Colombia)
articles_hidden.authors: Philip Riris; Natalia Lozada Mendieta; Heli Gaspar Morcote Rios
articles_hidden.abstract:
Abstract
This dataset contains high-resolution photographic imagery from sixteen rock art (pictograph) sites in the Serranía de La Lindosa (Guaviare Department, Colombia). The images were obtained during a single campaign of fieldwork in 2019, with the aim of producing three-dimensional reconstructions of painted rock art sites that are among the largest in the Americas in terms of numbers of motifs. The dataset contains the raw imagery, spatial information, associated dating information, and metadata related to this sample of sites in a simple hierarchical folder structure. Derivative data products, in the form of preliminary 3D modelling results, are provided through permalinks to a dedicated external webhost. The combined resource supports analysis, interpretation, reuse, and dissemination of these remarkable sites in a region of the world (lowland South America) where archaeological data availability is generally scarce. 

Resumen
Este conjunto de datos contiene imágenes fotográficas de alta resolución de 16 sitios de arte rupestre (pictografías) en la Serranía de La Lindosa (Departamento de Guaviare, Colombia). Las imágenes fueron obtenidas durante una única campaña de trabajo de campo en 2019, con el fin de producir reconstrucciones tridimensionales de algunos de los sitios de arte rupestre pintado más grandes de América en términos de número de motivos.
El conjunto incluye imágenes en formato RAW, información espacial, datos de datación asociados y metadatos relacionados con esta muestra de sitios, organizados en una estructura de carpetas jerárquica simple. Los productos de datos derivados, en forma de resultados preliminares de modelación 3D, se proporcionan mediante enlaces permanentes a un sitio web externo.
Este recurso combinado apoya el análisis, la interpretación, la reutilización y la gestión de estos sitios extraordinarios en las tierras bajas de Amazonía, donde la disponibilidad de datos arqueológicos es generalmente escasa.

articles_hidden.title: A Research Note on the pitfalls of sample selection and what (not) to control for in gender wage gap estimations
articles_hidden.authors: Matthias Collischon
articles_hidden.abstract: Estimating discriminatory gaps is one of the core topics of Sociology. A large number of studies use observational data to estimate these gaps, typically by controlling for potentially confounding factors and interpreting the coefficient of the group variable (e.g. female) as the degree of discrimination. However, estimations in this manner require choices both with regards to sample selection as well as the selection of variables to control for the stages where researchers assume discrimination to occur. Against the backdrop of the literature on gender wage gaps, this research note discusses these choices, their impact on the interpretation of the results and provides recommendations for applied researchers on how to deal with these choices in practice.

articles_hidden.title: El nombre de las cosas: denominaciones alimentarias, carne cultivada y el bajo costo de regular (de la legge di purezza italiana a la Ley N° 21.664 y al caso NotMilk ante la Corte Suprema)
articles_hidden.authors: Andrés Gabriel Varas Quijón
articles_hidden.abstract:
Italia prohíbe desde 1967 fabricar pasta seca con trigo blando y desde 2023 producir y
comercializar carne cultivada; Chile, que muchos suponen huérfano de reglas en la materia, es en realidad
pionero mundial del etiquetado frontal (Ley N° 20.606), acaba de definir por ley qué es «carne» y de vedar
esa denominación a lo que no lo es (Ley N° 21.664, vigente desde noviembre de 2025), y su Corte Suprema
resolvió en mayo de 2026 —invalidando de oficio la sentencia de alzada— la disputa más célebre del
continente sobre el nombre de un alimento: el caso NotMilk (rol N° 4.843-2024). Este trabajo reúne esas
piezas dispersas bajo una sola pregunta: ¿qué puede y qué debe hacer el derecho con el nombre de las cosas
que comemos? La respuesta se construye desde la jurisprudencia europea, que en 1988 (Drei Glocken) y en
2024 (Protéines France) dijo lo mismo con treinta y seis años de distancia: la protección del consumidor no
exige prohibir, exige nombrar — una denominación legal y una información completa bastan, y son la forma
más barata de regular que conoce el derecho. A esa luz se examinan la legge di purezza italiana y su límite
europeo, la prohibición italiana de la carne cultivada y su asedio, la arquitectura de la Ley N° 21.664 —que
elevó a rango legal, a costo cero, una definición que ya estaba en el Reglamento Sanitario—, la ratio del caso
NotMilk sobre actos de engaño, culpa y consumidor medio, y el limbo en que quedó la carne cultivada en
Chile: ni carne ni vegetal. El artículo propone, de lege ferenda, una denominación legal propia para los
alimentos de cultivo celular y una evaluación de inocuidad caso a caso, y cierra con un decálogo del
regulador prudente. La tesis: nomina sunt consequentia rerum — cuando la ley pone a cada alimento su
nombre exacto, el mercado hace el resto.

articles_hidden.title: Transformaciones del capital humano durante y al final de la transición demográfica
articles_hidden.authors: Nicolas Sacco
articles_hidden.abstract: Entre 2014 y 2024, Argentina experimentó la caída de fecundidad más rápida de su historia en paralelo a una expansión educativa masiva. Este artículo evalúa cómo la transición demográfica avanzada reconfigura el capital humano mediante el proceso por el cual cohortes más jóvenes y educadas reemplazan a las viejas y menos educadas. A través de la armonización de microdatos censales (1970-2022) y registros vitales, se describe más de medio siglo de historia educativa y se modelan escenarios prospectivos mediante modelos multi-estado hasta 2100. Los resultados muestran un aumento acelerado del nivel educativo promedio, situando al país en una posición regional intermedia y acercando a sus cohortes jóvenes a la composición de países desarrollados. No obstante, Argentina exhibe una convergencia incompleta con una marcada desigualdad interna, evidenciada por un desfase temporal de más de una década en la estructura educativa de las regiones del norte respecto de las áreas centrales. Las proyecciones muestran cómo el recambio por cohortes cerrará progresivamente estas brechas hacia 2050.

articles_hidden.title: Correcting molecular myopia in chemical risk governance: hormonal infrastructure as a conceptual lens
articles_hidden.authors: Taneli Rajala; Nina Janasik
articles_hidden.abstract: Widespread declines in human fecundity and biodiversity signal a creeping crisis that links to proliferating chemical pollution. Problematically, the risk governance of chemicals is mired with laboratory-level molecular knowledge that poorly matches with population-level threats arising from cumulative, chronic exposures to multiple borderline toxicants. We identify this molecular myopia as a fundamental misalignment between the scales at which chemical governance operates and the scales at which ecotoxicological research raises alarm—a misalignment reproduced in ongoing EU regulatory reforms despite their protective ambitions. In this conceptual work, we apply institutional theory and science and technology studies to explicate the key role of scale alignment in enabling effective governance intervention. Focusing on endocrine-disrupting chemicals, we develop the concept of hormonal infrastructure to highlight the cultural-cognitive level from which scale realignment must begin with chemical governance. This infrastructural lens foregrounds hormonal functions as vital and shared ecologies that require distributed human care to withstand diffuse chemical pollution. By reframing chemical risks as policy objects through infrastructures rather than through molecules, we make the case for a more prudential and multilevel form of precaution to address multichemical exposures that continue to slip through regulatory oversight.

articles_hidden.title: A Blended Distribution
articles_hidden.authors: George Y. Nie
articles_hidden.abstract: We use an example to show that a distribution is asymmetric generally, suggesting that extant statistic methodologies are problematic. Treating the force behind asymmetry as momentum, we define a distribution with momentum as a blended distribution—as if a normal distribution is disfigured by, or blended with, momentum. We propose that a variable’s movement over a period follows a distribution longitudinally while the literature is usually limited to a variable’s population that follows a distribution cross-sectionally. We introduce a methodology of mean expected number (MEN) of observations to measure the invisible observations of a distribution, thereby obtaining the probability density curve. We show that the probabilities predicted by a normal distribution are largely incorrect.

articles_hidden.title: A HISTÓRIA ECONÔMICA NO BRASIL
articles_hidden.authors: Thales Zamberlan Pereira
articles_hidden.abstract: Este artigo analisa aproximadamente 50 mil teses e dissertações defendidas em departamentos de história e economia ao longo das últimas quatro décadas, com o objetivo de mapear a evolução da história econômica no Brasil e oferecer um guia para o desenvolvimento da área. Antes da análise empírica, centrada no período 1980-2022, apresento um panorama histórico que cobre desde o surgimento dos estudos de caráter ensaístico, predominantes até a década de 1950, até o amadurecimento da produção acadêmica. Esse processo teve início na década de 1960 com a contribuição dos “brasilianistas” e consolidou-se a partir dos anos 1980, quando a expansão dos programas de pós-graduação em diferentes regiões do país firmou a pesquisa monográfica e especializada como padrão dominante da disciplina.

articles_hidden.title: Same Sullivan, different worlds: When prevalence is not health, and lifetables are not mortality
articles_hidden.authors: Tim Riffe; Rustam Tursun-zade; Octavio Bramajo
articles_hidden.abstract: Background: A lifetable combined with the prevalence of a health condition is sufficient to estimate health expectancy (HLE) using the Sullivan method. Different approaches exist for decomposing differences in HLE calculated this way. It has been suggested that such results cannot be interpreted directly, as they do not adequately disentangle health and mortality effects, with each estimated component potentially reflecting unobserved contributions from both processes. Objectives: Inspired by Anscombe’s quartet, we introduce a Sullivan analog to show that multistate systems with fundamentally different dynamics can yield identical Sullivan-based summary measures. Methods: We generate 32 multistate scenarios, 16 allowing for recovery (returns) and 16 without recovery, all of which exactly match the same values for prevalence, mortality, and by extension healthy life expectancy. We then perform all 240 valid pairwise multistate decompositions to assess whether differences across scenarios are detectable. Results: As expected, the multistate decompositions yield varied and meaningful effects from individual health and mortality hazards on health expectancy, all of which sum to zero at the margin. The analogous Sullivan decompositions all imply that prevalence and lifetable effects are both zero. Conclusions: These findings suggest that results derived from Sullivan-based decompositions are inherently ambiguous. Such results can be interpreted as prevalence and lifetable effects, but not as health and mortality effects, and interpretation must therefore be approached with caution.

articles_hidden.title: The Two Accountings of Gendered Violence: Criminal Order, Police Legitimacy, and Recorded Violence in Chicago
articles_hidden.authors: Igor Novaes Lins
articles_hidden.abstract: Women are a rising share of the people shot in Chicago, and the police series that should register violence against them moves with the structure of the city's criminal order. The paper follows both patterns across 77 community areas, 2010 to 2024, separating what armed territorial order does to violence from what it does to its record. The female share of shooting victims rises from about one in ten in the early 2010s to about one in six after 2022, and Cook County vital records, which never pass through a police station, reproduce the trend. The gender composition of victims is equivalent across gang identities within three percentage points, so what varies is volume. Where more gangs compete over the same ground, registered civilian-initiated violence rises by seven to nine percent per standard deviation of fragmentation, in domestic and non-domestic series alike, a movement at the institutional gateway. Under concentrated control, violence against women changes place. Their share of gunfire moves downward in every specification, with conventional confirmation in only one, while the male series stays flat. The domestic share of their homicides rises with concentration in every window, so consolidation pulls women out of the street's line of fire and leaves the violence against them at home, where the registered series shows no movement. The record of violence against women, these results imply, measures access to the state as much as harm, and the harm side requires a second, non-police accounting that the paper specifies as a concrete program.

articles_hidden.title: The Accountability Gap in Sub-Sovereign ESG Finance: A Case Study of Police Administration Oversight in Chiba Prefecture, Japan
articles_hidden.authors: Takashi Miyazawa
articles_hidden.abstract: This paper examines a critical vulnerability in the methodology of sub-sovereign ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) ratings, utilizing Chiba Prefecture, Japan, as a primary case study. While global ESG frameworks increasingly evaluate local government bonds, rating agencies predominantly rely on macro-level socioeconomic indicators and overarching policy frameworks, creating a significant "measurement gap." We demonstrate how this macro-dependence obscures micro-level governance failures—specifically, the indefinite suspension of complaint processing and the systemic non-creation of official records within police administration. By applying an axiomatic approach grounded in administrative law and corporate governance principles, this study empirically documents the existence of a structural "Accountability Gap" at the operational entry point. The findings highlight the critical need for institutional investors and ESG rating agencies to discount the reliability of sub-sovereign sustainability representations when auditable management evidence is structurally absent.

articles_hidden.title: Cloud Capital's Hidden Thirst: Scope 2 Water and the Geography of US Data Center Electricity
articles_hidden.authors: Atoshi Golder
articles_hidden.abstract: Data center operators report water use as a facility-level question, disclosing on-site metrics while omitting the water consumed in generating the electricity they purchase — their Scope 2 water footprint. This paper quantifies that omission at the eGRID-subregion level and traces its consequences for a standardized data center load. Comparing EPA eGRID 2018 against eGRID 2023 on an identical pipeline, I find that generation-weighted national water intensity fell 17.1% over the five years in which data center electricity demand accelerated, but that the decline was uneven: several subregions gaining generation share fell more slowly than the national average, and SERC Virginia/Carolina — host to the largest data center market in the world by inventory — fell only 7.7%, less than half the national pace. Combining eGRID generation data with consumption-basis water coefficients, I estimate a total of 1,350.6 billion gallons of operational water consumption embedded in contiguous-US electricity generation across all end uses in 2023, and show that an identical data center's embedded footprint varies approximately 3.2-fold by grid region under common technology-factor assumptions. I then construct a Water Dependency Index and adjust it by a territorial water-scarcity score built from the World Resources Institute's Aqueduct basin indicators, on the principle that identical consumption imposes different costs depending on where it occurs; the adjusted index ranks SERC Virginia/Carolina first in the nation. No widely adopted disclosure framework requires standardized, location-based reporting of electricity-embedded water. The paper proposes extending location-based Scope 2 carbon accounting, which is structurally analogous, to water.

articles_hidden.title: Theory of Carried Gaps in an Organizational Transformation
articles_hidden.authors: Jérôme Mendoza-Trussart
articles_hidden.abstract:
Organizational transformations are generally analyzed through change strategies, support mechanisms, resistance, or adaptation capacities. These approaches remain essential, but they sometimes leave a decisive question in the background: what happens to the gap between what the transformation requires and what the organization actually makes possible?

The Theory of Carried Gaps proposes that organizational gaps do not disappear when they are not addressed by the system. They can be displaced, absorbed, compensated for, and ultimately carried by individuals or collectives. Managers, experts, committed teams, or key actors then provide, often without an explicit mandate or proportionate recognition, the regulation necessary for continuity of activity.

The central contribution of the theory is to shift the focus: rather than considering only the difficulty experienced by an individual, it becomes possible to ask which organizational gap is being carried so that the system can continue to function. The managerial action then consists in making these gaps and their carrying mechanisms visible, enabling the organization to take back what it has left to individuals.

articles_hidden.title: Produção científica de um programa de educação ambiental no licenciamento federal: Análise bibliométrica do PEA-Pescarte
articles_hidden.authors: Vitor de Moraes Peixoto
articles_hidden.abstract:
O licenciamento ambiental federal obriga as operadoras de petróleo a financiar programas de educação ambiental, executados por universidades públicas ao longo de mais de uma década. Avalia-se o efeito socioambiental desses programas; não se mede o conhecimento que eles deixam. Este artigo faz esse levantamento para o PEA-Pescarte por revisão sistemática PRISMA 2020, que reúne acervo
institucional, auditoria de planilha e busca em três bases: 356 obras em 382 registros de 284 autores, descritas por cinco redes. articles_hidden.title: A POLÍTICA DE EXPANSÃO ECONÔMICA SIMBIÓTICA PULSANTE DOS ESTADOS UNIDOS: MECANISMOS DE INFLUÊNCIA GLOBAL E EXPLORAÇÃO DE RECURSOS ESTRANGEIROS
articles_hidden.authors: Juliano Paniago de Alcântara
articles_hidden.abstract:
O presente estudo propõe o modelo da “Política de Expansão Econômica Simbiótica
Pulsante” como arcabouço de análise da projeção de poder dos Estados Unidos no século
XXI, assim como do ordenamento temporal com que instrumentos coercitivos,
institucionais e persuasivos sustentam a internacionalização das corporações americanas.
A metodologia integra quatro estudos de caso (Iraque, América Latina, Ucrânia e Golfo
Pérsico), corroboração em painel país×ano e análise econométrica de séries 2000–2024
— cointegração, VECM, precedência de Granger, regressão bayesiana e reamostragem.
Os resultados identificam a precedência dos gastos militares sobre os retornos de
investimento direto no exterior como impulso de curto prazo direcionalmente robusto,
com defasagem de dois anos, sobreposto a um ciclo secular de renda mundial que domina
o longo prazo. Formaliza-se a “pulsação” como construto temporal falseável, distinto do
smart power, e reposiciona-se a política externa americana como mecanismo estrutural de
manutenção hegemônica.

articles_hidden.title: Bucks for Bumps: How Paid Parental Leave Pays Off for Firms
articles_hidden.authors: Hillary Cookler
articles_hidden.abstract: Firms use benefits such as paid parental leave (PPL) to attract and retain employees. In the U.S., which lacks broad public PPL benefits, firms increasingly provide this benefit. Systematic evidence of its benefits remains limited, due in part to the absence of comprehensive data on firm policies. Using a novel, hand-collected database of firm policy changes, this paper estimates the causal effect of PPL expansion on employee retention using a differences-in-differences approach. PPL expansions reduce departure rates by 3.1%, an effect equivalent to a permanent wage increase of 1.8%. Retention gains for women are concentrated among the lowest paid and those in the most junior roles, while retention gains for men are broad-based. At the firm level, retention gains concentrate in the interior of the internal labor market flexibility distribution and among firms with moderate firm-specific human capital, and they are robust to concurrent benefit changes and to firm revenue trajectories. Public PPL programs, by contrast, show no comparable retention effect, consistent with the non-portability of firm-provided benefits. Combining fertility estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) with worker and firm data, the paper calculates the expected costs of PPL provision and compares them to retention gains: at realistic utilization rates, PPL expansions generate positive net returns to firms.

articles_hidden.title: Evaluation of Initial Mental Health Impacts of Federal Changes in Identity Document Guidance on Transgender and Nonbinary Persons
articles_hidden.authors: Clair Kronk; Devin Madden; Rishabh Jain; Ashley Michelle Morales; Diddier Prada; Hill Wolfe; Carol R. Horowitz
articles_hidden.abstract:
Background: To assess potential mental health impacts of restrictions on gender marker changes by transgender and nonbinary people in the wake of Executive Order (EO) 14168. 
Methods: From March to July 2025, we surveyed transgender and nonbinary persons from a large northeastern medical system regarding gender markers on documents, current mental health status, and perspectives on current sociopolitical climate. 
Results: Quantitative analyses (n = 368) revealed identification as Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish and exploring one’s gender identity were related to greater distress. Gender marker change status on passports was associated with serious psychological distress, though this relationship was not statistically significant among other document types. Qualitative responses highlighted extensive concerns over mental wellbeing, political targeting, and staying in the U.S., while also showcasing perceived protective factors, and concluding with acknowledgement of transgender rights as human rights. 
Conclusions: Our findings describe a high rate of distress and pervasive fears tied to EO 14168 and the broader political environment.

articles_hidden.title: The Bank-Financed Margin of Trade Credit: Evidence from Italian Innovative and Ordinary SMEs
articles_hidden.authors: Angelo Leogrande; Mauro Di Molfetta; Valeria Nortarnicola; Maria Giovanna Trotta; Antonio Volpe Plantamura
articles_hidden.abstract:
Design/methodology/approach. The sample comprises 63,858 firm-year observations on 9,983 Italian innovative start-ups, innovative SMEs and ordinary SMEs between 2015 and 2024, drawn from statutory accounts. The collection period is regressed on bank debt with firm and year effects under nine estimators and six alternative scalings of both sides of the equation. A cluster analysis comparing six algorithms across eleven validity indices partitions the firms by financial configuration, and the equation is re-estimated within each group. Six regression learners fitted to the same demeaned data test the linearity and additivity restrictions the panel imposes.
Purpose. Trade credit and bank credit have been described as substitutes for three decades, yet a competing tradition finds them complementary, and the evidence has not converged. This paper argues that the disagreement is definitional rather than empirical. Almost every study measures trade credit received, treating the firm as a borrower choosing between two funding sources, while the credit the firm extends to its own customers enters as a control or not at all. The paper estimates both margins on one sample and asks whether bank borrowing lengthens or shortens the credit small and medium enterprises grant.
Findings. Bank indebtedness and the collection period move together within firms, at 0.48 days per percentage point of bank debt over turnover and positive under every estimator, while the same equation on payables returns −0.43. A model of a supplier facing a bank credit limit generates both signs from one first-order condition and bounds pass-through between zero and one, which the data satisfy at 0.126 euro per euro. The association reaches 0.81 among long-cycle firms, halves where liquidity is abundant, and declines from 0.80 to 0.50 across the decade as bank credit loosens.
Originality/value. The paper reconciles two literatures previously read as contradictory by estimating both margins of trade credit on one sample and deriving both signs from a single decision problem. It identifies a measurement problem the field has not addressed: because trade credit granted and bank debt are conventionally scaled by turnover, the estimated coefficient ranges from +0.48 to −0.12 across ratio specifications, so published estimates are not mutually comparable. It is also the first study of trade credit supply in the certified Italian populations of innovative start-ups and SMEs.

articles_hidden.title: “When I Turned 18, It All Ended”: Age Control, Migration Regimes and Radical Social Work
articles_hidden.authors: Nikoleta Gerontaki; Dimitra - Dora Teloni
articles_hidden.abstract:
* This is a post-peer-review, pre-copy edited version of an article published in Critical and Radical Social Work. The definitive publisher-authenticated version is available online at: Critical and Radical Social Work Journal https://doi.org/10.1332/20498608Y2026D000000141

What are the experiences of former unaccompanied minors in Greece in the process of transitioning to adulthood, what rights are infringed in the process, and how do their voices resist to silence and exclusion? Drawing on qualitative research conducted in 2024 with 10 young refugees, aged 18-22 years, based on semi-structured interviews analysed through thematic analysis, the article focuses on experiences of rights and social services from the perspective of radical social work. Findings demonstrate that the process of becoming an adult is frequently followed by loss of the basic services, which leaves dangerous conditions of living and infringement of the rights to housing, healthcare, education, and legal assistance. The participants' reflections on the policies in place show regret and gratitude for low levels of assistance, highlighting logics of deserving and undeserving care. Rights as a privilege at 18 years old become more akin to a right than an entitlement.

articles_hidden.title: I'm Dreaming of a Green Christmas:  Observational Loyalty Card Data Reveal the Health and Environmental Impacts of Festive Food Purchasing
articles_hidden.authors: Emma Wilkins; Alice Rose Kininmonth; Piyush Mohan; Mark Alan Green; Mark S Gilthorpe; Victoria Jenneson; Alexandra Johnstone; Michelle Morris
articles_hidden.abstract:
Background: The festive season is associated with weight gain that often persists into the new year, but the specific purchasing behaviours driving this are not well quantified. Christmas is also thought to be a period of disproportionate environmental impact, though the contribution from food purchasing has not been explored. The objective of this study was to use retail transaction data from a major UK supermarket to examine seasonal patterns in purchases of less healthy food and drink products (High in Fat, Sugar and/or Salt, HFSS), and the greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) from sales, and to quantify the extent to which purchasing behaviours during the festive period differ from the rest of the year.
Methods: Daily food and non-alcoholic beverage transaction data for 2022 for loyalty card holders living in Yorkshire and Humber were obtained from a major UK retailer. Products (>27,000) were classified as HFSS or non-HFSS using the UK Nutrient Profile Model and linked to GHGE estimates per kg. Changes in HFSS sales and GHGE were examined between the festive period (1-31 December 2022) and the baseline period (1 Jan-30 Nov 2022) using four metrics, expressed as the daily average over the two periods: HFSS sales (kg), percentage of all sales by weight that were HFSS (%HFSS), total GHGE from sales (kg-CO2-eq) and GHGE per kg (kg-CO2-eq·kg-1). 
Results: Marked increases in total HFSS sales and GHGE from sales were observed in the festive period (+25% and +15.3% respectively). The additional festive GHGE footprint was equivalent to 3,000 return flights from London to the North Pole. Consumers purchased proportionally more HFSS foods (+10.1%) and more foods with higher GHGE per kg (+6.6%). These changes were driven by shifts towards products that were both less healthy and more environmentally costly, particularly beef, chocolate and lamb.
Conclusion: Christmas is traditionally associated with generosity, celebration and plentiful food. Our study shows that this festive cheer comes at a cost to health and the environment. With a little more thought about what food we buy, the festive period can still be enjoyed while also benefiting population and planetary health.

articles_hidden.title: Female recreational runners’ perspectives of running-related injury risk and management: A qualitative exploration
articles_hidden.authors: Emily Authurs; Vivienne Chuter; Kim Hébert-Losier; Benjamin Peterson
articles_hidden.abstract:
Introduction: Recreational running enhances both mental and physical health. However, the high incidence of running related injury (RRI) is a key barrier to participation. Previous research has attempted to establish the risk factors for RRI, with the most well-established being previous injury and training errors. However, previous reductionist approaches for mitigating RRI risk factors have been largely unsuccessful, with interventions primarily focusing on isolated factors and not considering runners’ perceptions and experiences. 

Methods: We used an interpretive phenomenological analysis framework, qualitative data collection via focus groups, and reflexive thematic analysis to develop an understanding of the perceptions and experiences of female recreational runners in relation to RRI. Eleven female recreational runners were recruited across three focus groups to investigate participants’ perspectives and experiences relating to RRI risk, prevention, management, and health seeking behaviours. Each focus group was analysed using a six-phase reflexive thematic analysis approach to identify underlying themes. 

Results: Five interconnected themes (‘The Run’, ‘The Runner’, ‘The Injury’, ‘The Networks’, and ‘The Gear’) were identified as having an influence on whether a runner can remain injury-free, and the management of RRI. Analysis of runners’ perspectives and experiences cumulated in the development of the Perceptual RRI Risk, Prevention, and Management Nexus model. 

Conclusion: The female recreational runners interviewed particularly relied on informed self-regulation with guidance of past advice and previous experiences to manage RRI and identify RRI risk. The runners perceived modifiable and non-modifiable RRI risk factors should be considered when developing future injury prevention programs for runners like them.

articles_hidden.title: Policy Failure in Hong Kong's Waste Charging Scheme: A Bourdieusian, Critical Discourse, and Content Analysis
articles_hidden.authors: Alan
articles_hidden.abstract: This paper advances a field-theoretic framework for understanding policy implementation failure in hyper-dense, post-colonial cities when quantity-based waste charging is layered onto unreformed socio-spatial and institutional fields. Drawing on policy failure scholarship (McConnell, 2010a, 2010b; Bovens & 't Hart, 1996; Matland, 1995) and Bourdieu's practice theory, it demonstrates that Hong Kong's suspended Municipal Solid Waste Charging Scheme failed not from rejection of the polluter-pays principle, but from structural misalignment between a thin pricing instrument and the durable habitus of convenience disposal, ambiguous enforcement authority, and weak state symbolic capital. Three contributions follow. First, the field-restructuring precondition hypothesis: economic instruments in dense vertical cities require prior reconfiguration of infrastructure, institutional positions, and bodily hexis before pricing can function. Second, through comparison with Seoul, Taipei, Singapore and European PAYT schemes, Hong Kong's failure reflects an accelerated, compressed version of implementation challenges visible elsewhere when field transformation is elided. Third, preparatory measures—GREEN@Community infrastructure and Green$ incentives—generated unintended cultural and symbolic capital around recycling, creating a partial habitus shift despite the scheme's suspension, complicating linear narratives of policy failure. Environmental governance in dense Asian cities must be reconceptualised as long-term field restructuring rather than rapid behavioural levering.

articles_hidden.title: Imagining transformative pathways towards peaceful and equitable futures in the Korean peninsula
articles_hidden.authors: HyeJin Kim; Vitnia Lee; Hyeonjeong Kim; Miyoung Yeo; Yeoungjun Yeo; Youngcheol Cho; Gwanwoo Jin; Justin Johnson; Bohun Kang; Dirk N. Karger
articles_hidden.abstract: The Korean Peninsula faces the intertwined challenges of a polycrisis: an unresolved war and rapid development followed by demographic contraction, inequality, accelerating biodiversity loss, and intensifying climate risk. Achieving nature- and people-positive futures in this context requires finding alternative pathways: levers and actors of change, and their sequences and scaling. Citizens constructed transformative pathways from present-day Korea to four Korean Nature Futures visions. A methodology combined the Nature Futures Framework, Imagination Infrastructure, and Seeds of Good Anthropocene with narratives refined through the multi-level perspective and social-ecological systems theory. The four 2025-2050 pathways trace changes through five phases: present-day challenges, seeds of change, breaking points and shocks, and the emergence and stabilisation of new systems by 2050. Comparative analysis across ten domains – social, technological, ecological, economic, political, cultural, military, religious, identity, and the DMZ – identifies shared strategies and pathway-specific mechanisms. Across pathways, the DMZ is reimagined from a line of division into an anchor of ecological peace, with human and non-human actors recognised as agents of transformation. The study offers a transferable methodology for transformative scenario development in contested geopolitical settings and a proof of concept for anticipatory governance toward equitable and peaceful futures ‘Living in Harmony with Nature’.

articles_hidden.title: Gambling Industry Political Engagement, 2020–2026: A Proof-of-Concept for Auditing of Political Transparency Data using a GPT-assisted Pipeline.
articles_hidden.authors: James Close
articles_hidden.abstract:
Background: Commercial political activity is increasingly recognised within the broader framework of commercial determinants of health. However, UK gambling-related political engagement is fragmented across separate transparency systems. This study examined whether a GPT-assisted, independently reconciled workflow could integrate these records and provide a more complete picture of disclosed political activity.
Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted of UK gambling-related political engagement from 1 January 2020 to 25 August 2026 across three streams: (1) Electoral Commission political donations; (2) MPs’ declared hospitality/gifts and funded visits; and (3) ministerial meetings within the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport / Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS). GPT was used to retrieve, structure, link and classify records against a reference frame of gambling organisations, which was derived from multiple public sources, including Gambling Commission registers, Companies House records, company and trade-body information, and historical ownership and corporate-relationship evidence. After classification, each of the three streams underwent an independent GPT reconciliation pass, followed by bounded human adjudication of unresolved cases. A final audit compared the final donations and hospitality datasets with previous UK journalism and civil-society reporting.
Results: The principal analysis identified 127 donations with confirmed active commercial gambling connections, worth £7.73 million, from donors with a confirmed material commercial gambling connection active on the donation date. Of this value, 85.4% went to the Conservative political family and 13.0% to Reform UK. MPs declared 176 qualifying hospitality/gift events involving 71 MPs, worth £236,162, plus four funded visits. The ministerial-meeting census contained 272 gambling-related events, of which 86 involved principal commercial-industry actors. Across the 138-group company universe, meeting frequency was positively associated with both donation frequency (Spearman ρ=.390; p=.00004) and hospitality frequency (ρ=.487; p=.00001), although these associations are observational and non-causal. In the final audit against previously reported figures, 291 of the observed donation/hospitality records had no apparent or obvious match in the prior-reporting examined; and one genuine omission in this analysis was identified and corrected (related to hospitality). 
Conclusions: Systematic linkage across transparency systems revealed a scale and pattern of gambling-connected political activity that is not apparent from individual registers or prior headline reporting. GPT made this integration tractable, but independent reconciliation and human adjudication were essential. Integrated monitoring of political activity may therefore be important for understanding the commercial determinants of health in gambling and other harmful commodity industries.

articles_hidden.title: Tracking AI’s Scientific Anatomy: A Novel Framework for Analyzing the Use and Diffusion of AI in Science
articles_hidden.authors: Liangping Ding; Cornelia Lawson; Philip Shapira
articles_hidden.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) promises to transform science by accelerating knowledge discovery, automating processes, and introducing new paradigms for research.  However, there remains a limited understanding of how AI is being utilized in scientific research. In this paper, we develop a framework based on GPT-4 and SciBERT to identify AI’s role in scientific papers, differentiating between Foundational, Adaptation, Tool and Discussion modes of AI research. This allows us to capture AI’s diverse contributions, from theoretical advances to practical applications and critical analysis. We examine AI’s trajectory across these modes by analyzing time series, field-specific, and country trends. This approach expands on search-term based identification of AI contributions and offers insights into how AI is being deployed in science.

articles_hidden.title: A Fork in the Road for Global AI Governance: To Repair or Reconfigure Expert-Led Governance?
articles_hidden.authors: Adam McCarthy; Olajide Olugbade
articles_hidden.abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a live object of global governance, with expert-led institutional arrangements emerging across an international regime complex. While scholarship on epistemic communities and science-policy interfaces treats expertise as a mechanism for coordination under uncertainty, recent work in Objectual International Relations (O-IR) and Science and Technology Studies foregrounds knowledge politics, contested authority, and the co-productive character of governance. We bring these perspectives into conversation with AI governance through a reflexive workshop design using Nominal Group Technique, drawing on two expert workshops in the UK and US.
Findings show that expert panels remain valued for structuring debate, coordinating knowledge, and lending legitimacy to policy action. Yet participants identified tensions around exclusion, elite and private capture, weak accountability, geopolitical constraints, and temporal misalignment between institutional processes and technological change. An object-centered analysis further shows that AI remains an unstable governance object; the knowledge required to govern it is contested and unevenly distributed; and expertise itself is politically charged and institutionally unsettled. We synthesize these tensions into two pathways: Repair and Reconfiguration. Repair seeks to stabilize AI as a governable object, standardize relevant knowledge, and secure expert authority through institutional continuity and procedural refinement. Reconfiguration seeks to keep AI contested, broaden credible forms of knowledge, and reshape expertise through participation, reflexivity, and engagement with politics. The framework provides a critical lens for assessing emerging institutional designs for global AI governance and the trade-offs they entail.
